                       UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                           
6                    WESTERN DISTRICT OF WASHINGTON                           
                               AT SEATTLE                                     
7                                                                             
     UNITED STATES OF AMERICA,       CASE NO. C25-5307-KKE                    
8                                                                             

                   Plaintiff(s),     ORDER GRANTING MOTION FOR STAY           
9                                                                             
          v.                                                                  

10                                                                             
     DEEP RIVER LANDING, LLC, et al.,                                         

11                                                                             
                    Defendant(s).                                             

12                                                                             
         On October 7, 2025, Plaintiff United States of America requested a stay of the entire case 
13                                                                             
    due to a lapse in appropriations to the Department of Justice.  Dkt. No. 36 at 2.   
14                                                                             
         “A district court has discretionary power to stay proceedings in its own court[.]”  Lockyer 
15                                                                             
    v. Mirant Corp., 398 F.3d 1098, 1109 (9th Cir. 2005) (citing Landis v. N. Am. Co., 299 U.S. 248, 
16                                                                             
    254 (1936)).  In determining whether a stay is appropriate, the Court weighs the “competing 
17                                                                             
    interests which will be affected by the granting or refusal to grant a stay[,]” including:  
18                                                                             
         the possible damage which may result from the granting of a stay, the hardship or 
19        inequity which a party may suffer in being required to go forward, and the orderly 
         course of justice measured in terms of the simplifying or complicating of issues, 
20        proof, and questions of law which could be expected to result from a stay.   
21   Lockyer, 398 F.3d at 1110 (quoting CMAX, Inc. v. Hall, 300 F.2d 265, 268 (9th Cir. 1962)). 
22        In light of the lapse in appropriations to the Department of Justice, which represents 
23   Plaintiff in this case, and given that Defendants do not oppose Plaintiff’s motion (see Dkt. No. 36), 
24   the Court concludes that a temporary stay is warranted in this case.  Because Defendant’s motion 
1   to dismiss is pending, the Court has not yet entered a case schedule in this matter.  See Dkt. No. 
2   19.                                                                       
3        Accordingly, the Court GRANTS Plaintiff’s motion to stay the case in its entirety.   

4        Plaintiff  shall  notify  Defendants  and  the  Court  within  2  days  of  the  restoration  of 
5   appropriations and the Court will lift the stay at that time.  Plaintiff shall further advise the Court 
6   as soon as possible whether extension of any impacted deadlines is necessary.   
7        Dated this 8th day of October, 2025.                                 
8                                                                             
                                  A                                           
9                                                                             
                                  Kymberly K. Evanson                         
10                                 United States District Judge
